newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss executive pay rises but Germans still rule.
newsitem.headline: Swiss executive pay rises but Germans still rule.

text.p: A top Swiss manager earns a gross salary of 244,000 Swiss francs ($167,000) on average, but still tends to make less than a counterpart in Germany, Austria or Denmark, according to a study released on Wednesday.

Executives' pay rose an average 2.7 percent in the year to March 1997, in line with pay hikes in the prior year, the study of 1,975 executives at 165 industrial companies by consultants Keleinbaum und Partner and the HandelsZeitung newspaper found.

It divided executives into four categories, with those in the first group having most responsibility and earning an average 244,000 francs. The other groups earned 165,000, 122,000 and 93,000 a year, respectively.
"Heads of the sales, distribution, marketing or research and development departments or those in charge of commercial and technical operations earned the most among executives," it said.

A review of companies with 250 to 500 employees showed top managers earned gross pay of 265,000 francs in Switzerland, compared with 355,000 francs in Germany, 308,000 in Austria and 288,000 in Denmark.
"Top executives in Ireland, Britain, Italy and the Netherlands had to be satisfied with lower salaries," it said.
